title: Learning film scoring while keeping the band
summary: Interested in film scoring, he did arranging and orchestrating off and on but no composition until about 1958.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Yes, I became interested in, you know, in wanting to know more about film scoring, and more about composition, which I had not studied to that time. And ... but I worked with Alfred

Newman, and, oh -- with other music directors for a number of years, you know, off and on, doing arrangements -- arranging and some orchestrating. But I didn't do any actual composition until quite some years later, which would take us up to around 1958.
Uh huh. That's moving a bit too fast.
Did you get some additional film work shortly after "Stormy Weather", or was there a gap in there, and you continued with your band, and toured and so on?
Well, it was kind of spotty, you know. I did continue going out with the band, and I would come back and people would know of my availability, and would call me.
But it was just off and on, you know, because I was still interested in keeping the band together, if at all possible.
Right. But you have not yet decided to make a switch from one thing to another.
Several things were going on at once?
The more the merrier, in a sense.
Did you particularly try to understand film music? I guess as each project came up, you had to understand what you were doing?
Yes. Oh, yes. I was trying to figure it all out.
